answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes each agent identity expensive to fake: to join the market, an agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, like a ship paying harbor fees before it may dock. New identities start with zero trust and earn it slowly through verified work, so an attacker spinning up a comet-swarm of sock puppets pays real capital per identity, while honest agents, rooted like yarrow in one place, accumulate cheap, durable reputation. Forging a thousand credible histories costs far more than any single fraud gains.
